about: The viewpoints the sample is judged by. Tools/frames.py draws each with no window and compares it against the frame recorded beside it in Tools/frames/. A recorded frame changes only with a reason in the CHANGELOG — the picture is meant to change when the renderer does, and the point is that somebody looked. A frame may carry a tolerance of its own: the default is sized for a lit scene, and a flat drawing needs a far tighter one to catch anything at all.

frames.name: ruins-from-above
frames.shows: the sun's cascades, six lamps casting into the atlas and cubes, the braziers' embers, the tone map

frames.name: ruins-lintel
frames.shows: the lintel a body walks under, the stairs and the lift, normal-mapped stone and timber at eye height

frames.name: courtyard
frames.shows: the courtyard by day: the slider, the crates' emission, the towers, shadows across an open floor

frames.name: courtyard-turntable
frames.shows: the turntable, whose plan is a disc, and the stop crate beside the slider's run

frames.name: splash
frames.shows: the engine's mark, at the middle of its hold: the aim, the muzzle, the path carried off it, the impact — and the name under it in two tones. Drawn without the version line, which changes every release
